newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals mixed after firm open.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals mixed after firm open.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were mixed early Thursday, after a firmer than expected opening, but some funds were seen turning buyers in gold, while platinum group metals held up well after news Russia/Japan supply contract talks may resume next week.
* COMEX June gold was down 80 cents at $342.50, after seeing a $344.10-342.10 early range.

* Some funds and commission houses were seen on the bid in COMEX gold after the contract bounced well off its new contract low late Wednesday, suggesting support at the near four year lows seen in January may hold, analysts said.

* Gold had been trading in narrow ranges between $348 and $358 in the past month, but the breach of the bottom of this range Tuesday, along with lower than expected U.S. March CPI data, encouraged heavy fund selling, traders said.
* In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $340.20/70, compared to the London Thursday morning fix at $341.20 and the New York close Wednesday around $341.00/50.
* Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer reiterated comments made Thursday by German Finance Minister Waigel, saying Germany opposed central bank or IMF gold sales.
But he added it was not yet clear whether European central bank gold reserves would be transferred to the reserves of the planned European central bank under European Monetary Union.
European central banks hold about 14,300 tonnes of gold (460 million ounces), over 40 percent of all official world reserves.
COMEX May silver was down 7.0 cents at $4.700, after revisiting the three month lows seen in early April on Tuesday.
* NYMEX July platinum was up $1.20 at $373.00, while the October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread edged higher to $25.50 from $24.90 Wednesday.
* NYMEX June palladium was up $1.00 at $152.00, despite news that a team of Russian central bankers would visit Japan next week to resume talks on Russian/Japanese supply contracts.

* Short term platinum lease rates jumped to about six percent early Thursday, with Swiss houses seen big borrowers, but short term palladium lease rates were said to be still firm around 8-10 percent for one month and 6-8 percent for three months.
